Thanks again for the demo earlier today. A couple of follow-up items from our security and procurement side so we can scope the POC properly:

- Confirmation of in-transit and at-rest encryption standards you use (TLS / cipher suites, KMS envelope encryption algorithm).
- Options for customer-managed keys: can we bring our own keys (BYOK) and host in our own KMS/HSM? If yes, what are the supported flows and limitations?

Thanks,
Jamal

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: FinHaven - encryption and keying follow-up (POC)

Jamal —

Great to connect. Summary / quick answers up front, then proposed next steps.

Short answers
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3) with AEAD ciphers (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 or stronger).
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM for stored model caches and object storage; all keys wrapped using envelope encryption.
- BYOK: supported. Two patterns: (A) Cloud KMS integration (you provide keys in your cloud KMS and we reference them via a grant/role), (B) HSM-backed import/wrapping (we support AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and customer HSMs via KMIP in our Private deployment).
- Auditing: request-level metadata (request id, model id, timestamp) is logged. Payloads are never stored in plaintext in logs; we can configure redaction/hash of user identifiers. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM over a TLS syslog/HTTPS forwarder. Retention is configurable per-customer (default 90 days).
- Residency: production compute can be pinned to eu-west-1; backups remain in-region unless you opt into cross-region DR (opt-in only).

Attachments: I attached a short Redwood KMS options overview.

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive w/ Soojin (our crypto engineer) and Marissa (security/compliance) to walk the BYOK flows and the procurement checklist (30–45m).
2) We’ll provide a one-page procurement checklist + a proposed timeline for a Private deployment BYOK path.
3) If you confirm BYOK path, we will produce an evidence pack (SOC2 summary + KMS integration steps + sample audit logs) for procurement.

Availability: we have slots Tues/Wed this week in the EU morning. Which day works?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: FinHaven - encryption and keying follow-up (POC)

Jamal / team —

Following on Olga's note, a few technical details you can share with your security team. I kept it high level but with concrete implementation notes.

1) BYOK patterns we support\- Cloud KMS reference (recommended path for hosted Redwood): you create the CMEK in your cloud provider (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS) and grant Redwood a restricted key‑usage role that allows envelope encryption operations. Redwood never stores the unwrapped key material; we call the KMS to unwrap/wrap per key operation. This supports key rotation and audit records appear in your KMS logs.

- Pros: low ops for you, integrates with your existing key lifecycle and rotation policies.
- Cons: requires IRSA/role config and network connectivity to your KMS endpoint.

2) HSM / dedicated key boundary (Private deployment only)\- If you need an explicit HSM boundary under your control, we support mounting an HSM (KMIP or CloudHSM) that performs all wrap/unwrap inside your HSM. Redwood will configure a key‑wrapping adapter; unwrapped plaintext never crosses the HSM boundary.

- Supported vendors: AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, Thales nShield via KMIP bridge.
- Note: This path requires additional provisioning lead time (2–6 weeks) and an ops playbook for key import/processes.

3) Key import & rotation\- We support importing RSA/ECC symmetric key material for initial seeding (secure import tokens) and recommend using envelope keys (DEK wrapped by KMS CMKs). Rotation is compatible with both modes; we expose rotation hooks and maintain a key version map in our control plane.

4) Logging & telemetry\- Redwood logs request metadata (request id, model, route) and a hashed user identifier by default. We can:
  • Disable telemetry for specific routes (PII-only routes)
  • Send full structured logs to your SIEM endpoint over TLS with mutual auth
  • Configure retention windows per customer (30/90/365 days)

Implementation notes attached for your cloud team — includes sample IAM policies, network egress rules, and an example key grant flow.

[attachment: kms-integration-implementation-notes.md (14KB)]

If this aligns, Olga / Priyom will follow up with the procurement checklist and a proposed timeline for the BYOK-enabled POC. Happy to join the deep-dive.

— Soojin
Crypto & Platform Security, Redwood Inference
